title: Principal completeness detected by an invertible product differential
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme with its small pro-etale site [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $a$ be a global section for which multiplication on $R$ is monic. Work in the unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $F$ be any canonical universal principal quotient-completion model with its normalized unit [def-pur-principal-quotient-completion-model]. For every module sheaf $M$, the unit $M[0]\to F(M[0])$ is invertible if and only if the map $d_M=1-s_a$ on $\prod_{n\in\mathbb N}M$ is invertible, where $\operatorname{pr}_n s_a=a_M\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$ and $a_M$ denotes multiplication by $a$. Products and this differential are the explicit constructions of [lem-sfb-countable-scalar-difference-closure].

source.place: Definition 3.4.1 and Lemma 3.4.12 (1) iff (2), printed pp.20-23; Proposition 3.1.11, printed p.17

proof.text: Take the natural fibre triangle of [lem-sfb-regular-principal-completion-fiber]. Uniqueness of the left-derived functor identifies its completion model with F. On a K-flat resolution the representative counits are invertible; unit_computes and the normalized Roos coordinates show that the comparison preserves units. Natural K-flat resolution comparisons then give the same assertion for every derived object.

The first vertex of a distinguished triangle vanishes exactly when its second arrow is invertible; this follows also from [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] and the derived localization. Thus completeness means vanishing of the localized scalar Roos complex.

Exact countable products [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] compute this Roos complex on M[0] directly. Its only terms are the countable powers of M in degrees zero and one, with differential minus d_M, using the formula of [lem-sfb-countable-scalar-difference-closure]. Its two homology objects are kernel and cokernel of d_M. All vanish exactly when d_M is monic and epic, hence invertible in the abelian module category.

theorem complete_product_criterion
    (T : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{t})
    (R : Sheaf (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology T) CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)}
      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology T) R))]
    (a : (SheafOfModules.unit (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology T) R)).sections)
    (_ha : Mono (globalSectionMultiplication R a))
    (F : Model.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), w} R a)
    (M : ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)}
      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology T) R)) :
    IsIso (F.unit.app ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M)) ↔
      IsIso ((CountableScalarDifference.difference
        (PrincipalCompletionFiber.scalar R a)).app M)
